Autonav R1

Designed by theretroexe for the Autonomous Navigation Challenge. Drag to orbit, right-drag to pan, scroll to zoom, hover a part to name it.

Start here

Everything you need to build the robot is on this page. Download the files, print the plates in order, then follow the assembly steps below.

Download build files (.zip, 5.2 MB)

The zip has a Bambu Studio project with the 8 plates already laid out (autonav_plates_BambuStudio.3mf), every part as an STL for other slicers, print notes (PRINT_PLATES.md), and a 3D model plus dimension sheet (autonav_robot.obj, autonav_robot.md) in mm.

    Print plate 0 first and push its pins into its holes. If they're too tight or too loose, sort that out before printing the rest: every pin and joint uses the same clearance. Use 0.12 mm layers for the gears (plate 5). Have ready: superglue, double-sided tape, hot glue, a rubber band and a little grease.

    Assembly, step by step

    Drag the slider or use the buttons to build the robot one step at a time. New parts drop in highlighted.

      Still to confirm

      Motor RPM is unknown, so the 36:11 drive ratio is a reprintable pinion and crown. Print a test of each servo horn first: their splines are printed (25-tooth MG996R, 21-tooth SG90) and the fit is one setting in robot.py. Unmeasured: MG996R flange height and the Brio clip. Print snap pins, standoffs, horns and differential gears in PETG; tyres in TPU; the rest in PLA. Printed masses are estimates, so weigh the real parts.
